title: Karmelo Anthony seeks $250K for murder appeal as questions persist over family’s previous $634K fundraiser
text:

Anthony was convicted last week in the fatal stabbing of Frisco teenager Austin Metcalf during a high school track meet and was sentenced to 35 years in prison. The newly released exhibits provide the public with a closer look at the evidence that jurors considered before reaching their verdict.

Karmelo Anthony’s family is seeking another $250,000 to fund his appeal after an earlier campaign raised nearly $634,000 and faced questions over how the money was spent, the family announced at a news conference in Dallas, Texas.

The fundraising push came nearly two weeks after a judge denied Anthony’s request for a new trial. His family and supporters, including attorney Russell Wilson, used the Dallas news conference to outline the appeal.

Anthony, 19, was sentenced to 35 years in prison in June after a jury convicted him of murdering 17-year-old Austin Metcalf during a high school track meet in Frisco, Texas. He has appealed and says he cannot afford to hire an attorney for the appeal.

ANOTHER LAWYER JOINS KARMELO ANTHONY'S APPEAL AS KILLER CLAIMS HE CANNOT PAY FOR COUNSEL

The new fund is intended to cover legal fees, experts and other costs associated with challenging Anthony’s conviction, Wilson said.

Left: Karmelo Anthony is seen in a prison mugshot. Right: Austin Metcalf, who was stabbed to death by Anthony. (Texas Department of Criminal Justice; Jeff Metcalf)

"I think there's a misconception that the motion for new trial denial would have ended an appeal," Wilson said. "It actually is part of an appeal."

KARMELO ANTHONY BLASTS JUDGE IN NEW FILING OVER HANDLING OF MURDER TRIAL

Wilson said the appeal could take more than a year. The trial record is expected to be assembled in October. After that, both sides will make their case in writing, and the Dallas Court of Appeals could hold a hearing.

SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST TRUE CRIME NEWS

The request follows a GiveSendGo campaign launched on Anthony’s behalf in April 2025 that raised $633,908 before it was removed from public view following his conviction.

KARMELO ANTHONY CLAIMS HE'S PENNILESS AS BUSINESS RECORDS TIED TO PARENTS DRAW SCRUTINY

Karmelo Anthony's mother, Kayla Hayes, speaks at a press conference in April. (Next Generation Action Network via Facebook)

The earlier campaign was organized by Anthony’s mother and initially set a fundraising goal of nearly $1.4 million. Organizers said donations could be used for legal defense, moving the family, basic living expenses, transportation, counseling and security.

GiveSendGo said the money had been distributed over the previous year for lawful purposes, including legal defense and moving the family, and that the campaign was closed after its stated purpose was completed.

LISTEN: AUSTIN METCALF FAMILY FACING THREATS, FINANCIAL STRAIN AS KARMELO ANTHONY FUNDRAISING DRAWS SCRUTINY

The new campaign page says donations will be deposited into an attorney trust account administered by Wilson and that Anthony’s family will not receive or control the money. The page says the funds will be used only for legal expenses, including filings, transcripts, investigators and experts.

Demonstrators showed support for Karmelo Anthony outside the Collin County Courthouse in McKinney, Texas, on the first day of jury selection in his trial on June 1, 2026. (Derek Shook for Fox News Digital)

The page listed a $250,000 goal and $30,194 raised when viewed by Fox News Digital. Trinicia Ricks is identified as the campaign’s creator, while Wilson is listed as the person who will receive the funds.

KARMELO ANTHONY SUPPORTER REPORTEDLY FIRED AS OTHER BACKERS FACE BACKLASH OVER VERDICT REMARKS

A reporter pressed Dominique Alexander, a civil rights activist who has served as a spokesman for Anthony’s family, about the new request and what happened to money raised through the earlier campaign. The reporter also asked about claims that donations were used to buy a car or house.

FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X

"These are deliberate lies," Alexander said. "Why would we ask the question to a family to answer something that clearly was a lie?"

AUSTIN METCALF'S FAMILY HIT WITH DEATH THREATS AS KARMELO ANTHONY SUPPORTERS FACE VIOLENCE ALLEGATIONS

When asked where the previous money went, Alexander declined to explain the family’s fees or say whether any funds remained.

The GiveSendGo page for the Karmelo Anthony Legal Fund lists a $250,000 goal and $30,194 raised. (GiveSendGo)

Alexander said the original fundraiser also helped the family relocate after they faced threats.

LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST

"That fund was established to not only help with the legal process, but also be able to relocate this family to safety," he said.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE

Public records reviewed by Fox News Digital previously showed Anthony’s parents, Andrew Anthony III and Kala Hayes, were connected to business entities in Louisiana and Texas. A Texas entity listing Andrew Anthony III as its registered agent became active 24 days after Metcalf’s death.

SEND US A TIP

The records did not show whether either company generated revenue, held assets or received money from the fundraiser. Anthony’s parents have not been accused of wrongdoing.

GOT A TIP?

Anthony has since described himself in court filings as a "penniless, destitute, and indigent person, too poor to employ counsel to represent me on the appeal."

GET BREAKING NEWS BY EMAIL

Wilson declined to provide additional details about the defense strategy, saying some issues could become important in future proceedings.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Anthony remains in custody while the appeal moves forward.

Fox News Digital has reached out to Wilson for comment.
